source.title: Low-loss connection of weight vectors: distribution-based approaches

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-set accuracy for trained networks on CIFAR and tests low-loss connections between trained endpoints. The endpoint results bear on V1, though the study is not designed to map training-to-zero conditions.
record.gate_note: Most reported results concern accuracy along connection paths, which does not measure the claim versions. The endpoint training accuracies in Tables 1 and 2 and the VGG16 results bear on V1. Do not treat the path-accuracy comparisons as training-error results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own SGD-trained convolutional networks' training classification accuracy on CIFAR-10, directly bearing on V1. Its main connection-path experiments do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that distribution-based methods construct low-loss connections, with more detailed and computationally complex methods generally performing better. They also demonstrate weight-adjustment ensembling. They do not conclude when SGD reaches near-zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains networks to create endpoints, then evaluates paths connecting them; it does not compare recipes for reaching near-zero training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set endpoint accuracy varies across the reported architectures and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected endpoints attain 70.60% and 95.13% training accuracy on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected networks can retain substantial training error under this SGD recipe.

record.problems: Endpoint training accuracies are secondary to the study's connection-path objective. The VGG16 table entry prints uncertainty as '± 0.'; the supplied text does not provide the missing precision.
record.rows_left_out: Connection-path accuracy results in Tables 1–4 and figures are not training-error outcomes and do not measure a behavior named by the claim versions. MNIST endpoint accuracy is outside the stated CIFAR scope of V1.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100 training accuracy, Adam, early stopping, and controlled convolutional-network size or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with convolutional depth and matched shortcut comparisons.
Initialization comparisons, learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and divergence.
Matched normalization comparisons, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Connection-path accuracy measures constructed paths between trained endpoints, not gradient training success or avoidance of spurious minima. Dense-network depth comparisons report test accuracy and therefore do not test V3. Training VGG16 without batch normalization alone does not test V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, Adam, early stopping, and systematic comparisons of model size or training duration are not tested.
